message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of the most highly‑rated **crime‑thrillers** released (or made available) in 2020—whether they hit theaters before the pandemic shut down cinemas, premiered at festivals, or landed directly on streaming platforms. All of them earned praise for tight plotting, strong performances, and atmospheric tension.

| # | Title & Release Platform | Director(s) | Why It Stands Out |
|---|---------------------------|-------------|--------------------|
| 1 | **“Tenet” – *Warner Bros.* / Netflix** | Christopher Nolan | Though technically more of a sci‑fi action film, its intricate heist plot, mind‑bending time manipulation, and relentless pacing make it one of the decade’s most cerebral thrillers. Critics lauded its audacious narrative structure and high production values. |
| 2 | **“Uncut Gems” – *Netflix*** | Josh Safdie & Benny Safdie | A frenetic plunge into New York City’s diamond trade, starring Adam Sandler as a charismatic jeweler whose gambling addiction spirals out of control. Its razor‑sharp editing and palpable dread keep viewers glued until the very end. |
| 3 | **“The Irishman” – *Netflix*** | Martin Scorsese | While primarily a gangster epic, this long‑form crime drama delivers tense courtroom scenes, moral ambiguity, and masterful use of de-aging tech. Scorsese’s direction turns a sprawling saga into a taut psychological study. |
| 4 | **“Mank” – *HBO Max* (also theatrical)** | David Fincher | Set against the backdrop of Hollywood’s Golden Age, “Mank” follows screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz as he battles studio politics while crafting *Citizen Kane*. Fincher’s meticulous mise‑en‑scène and period authenticity create a moody noir atmosphere. |
| 5 | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7” – *Netflix*** | Aaron Sorkin | Although rooted in political protest rather than conventional crime, the film’s legal intrigue, sharp dialogue, and ensemble cast deliver a gripping courtroom thriller that feels both timely and timeless. |
| 6 | **“A Quiet Place Part II” – *Universal Pictures*** | John Krasinski | Not strictly a crime story but its suspenseful build‑up, inventive sound design, and emotional stakes elevate it beyond typical horror. The sequel’s cat-and-mouse chase through post‑apocalyptic landscapes keeps audiences on edge. |
| 7 | **“The Invisible Man” – *Amazon Prime Video*** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of H.G. Wells’ classic, this film blends science fiction with domestic terror. Its claustrophobic setting and subtle hints of supernatural menace culminate in a nail‑biting climax. |

### How These Films Were Received

| Film | Rotten Tomatoes Score | Metacritic Rating | Key Praise |
|------|-----------------------|------------------|------------|
| Tenet | 70% | 71/100 | Complex storytelling, visual spectacle |
| Uncut Gems | 84% | 78/100 | Intense character arc, kinetic energy |
| The Irishman | 94% | 88/100 | Masterclass in filmmaking, stellar cast |
| Mank | 93% | 86/100 | Period detail, compelling screenplay |
| The Trial of the Chicago 7 | 95% | 83/100 | Powerful script, historical relevance |
| A Quiet Place Part II | 92% | 80/100 | Tension building, effective silence |
| The Invisible Man | 91% | 77/100 | Innovative twist, chilling atmosphere |

> **Tip:** If you’re looking for something less mainstream, check out indie gems like *"The Last Black Man in San Francisco"* (though more drama), which still carries a gritty undercurrent of crime and social critique.

Enjoy your binge‑watch!
